exam.dsh.purpose: university admission; DSH-2 is the usual requirement

scenes.pageTitle: {n} everyday German conversations to practise, A1 to C2
scenes.description: Role-play scenes for speaking German: the bakery, the doctor on the phone, the citizens' office, a flat viewing, a job interview, a parents' evening, a complaint to the landlord - who you are, who you talk to, Sie or du, and the opening line, A1 to C2.
scenes.lead: Each scene is a real situation with a role for you, a role for the tutor, a register (Sie or du) and facts the other person knows - the price of the rolls, the opening hours, what the landlord wants. In the app the tutor plays the other person, keeps to the facts and corrects you at the end, never mid-flow.

learn.weeksAtLevel: The course below is {n} weeks at this level; a week is about an hour a day.
learn.indexTitle: Learn German from A1 to C2: a guided course, week by week
learn.indexDescription: A {n}-week German course from A1 to C2, built from the official exam syllabi: what each level means, how long it takes, and every week's grammar, words, scenes and tutor questions. Free to read; the app teaches it.
learn.indexH1: German from A1 to C2, week by week
learn.indexLead: The Eszett course is {n} weeks across six levels. Every week has a goal you can say in one sentence, two or three grammar cards, a word field, a scene to play, something to read and listen to, a writing task and a check. The whole plan is here to read; the app is where a tutor teaches it to you.
learn.levelsMean: The levels are those of the Common European Framework (CEFR). In Germany they are not abstract: A1 is the certificate for the spouse visa, B1 the one for the settlement permit, naturalisation and the end of the integration course, B2 what most employers and vocational training places ask for, C1 the door to university. The Goethe-Institut's guidance is {a2} to reach A2, {b1} for B1, {b2} for B2 and {c1} for C1 - with a tutor in your pocket and an hour a day, a level is a few months.
learn.howWeek.1: Words of the week's field, with gender and plural, read aloud by the phone.
learn.howWeek.2: Grammar cards: the rule in your language and in German, examples, the typical mistakes - [all {n} are here](grammar).
learn.howWeek.3: Drills on exactly those rules, checked against the dictionary, not guessed.
learn.howWeek.4: Ask the tutor the questions learners ask at this point - and your own.
learn.howWeek.5: Read and listen: a short text and a dialogue, then questions.
learn.howWeek.6: Speak: a [scene](scenes) with the tutor as the other person, then one of your own.
learn.howWeek.7: Write the kind of text the exams ask for, and get it corrected.
learn.howWeek.8: Check: a short test on the week; pass it and the next week opens.
learn.examsAlong: Each level page names the exams at that level - [Goethe, telc, the DTZ, TestDaF, DSH and ÖSD compared](exams) - and the app has timed mock oral exams for every one of them.
level.A1.name: Beginner
level.A1.can: You understand and use everyday expressions and very simple sentences: introduce yourself, ask where someone lives and what they do, order in a café, buy a ticket, fill in a form - if the other person speaks slowly and is willing to help.
level.A1.examsNote: Goethe-Zertifikat A1: Start Deutsch 1, telc Deutsch A1 and ÖSD Zertifikat A1 are the exams at this level; the A1 certificate is what the German family-reunification visa asks for.
level.A2.name: Elementary
level.A2.can: You handle routine exchanges about familiar things: shopping, work, family, your neighbourhood, a doctor's appointment, a short e-mail to a friend. You can describe your background and immediate needs in simple terms.
level.B1.name: Intermediate - the level Germany asks for
level.B1.can: You follow the main points of clear standard speech on work, school and leisure, cope with most situations while travelling, write connected text on familiar topics, describe experiences and plans and give reasons. B1 is the level of the integration course's final exam (DTZ) and of the settlement permit and naturalisation.
level.B2.name: Upper intermediate - work and vocational training
level.B2.can: You understand the main ideas of complex texts, including technical discussion in your field, speak fluently enough for a normal conversation with native speakers, and write clear, detailed texts arguing a point of view. B2 is what most employers, vocational training programmes and many professional recognitions ask for.
level.C1.name: Advanced - university
level.C1.can: You understand demanding, longer texts and implicit meaning, speak spontaneously and fluently without obvious searching for words, and write well-structured text on complex subjects. C1 is the usual requirement for German-language university study (TestDaF 4, DSH-2, Goethe C1, telc C1 Hochschule).
level.C2.name: Mastery
level.C2.can: You understand practically everything you read or hear, summarise information from several spoken and written sources with reasons and explanations, and express yourself spontaneously, very fluently and precisely, bringing out finer shades of meaning.
level.C2.hours: at least 1,000 lessons in total (Goethe-Institut guidance)
